text: Sider's heavyweight realism holds that ontological disputes are substantive because:
choices: ordinary conceptual rules together with uncontested empirical facts settle them easily.
reality has a mind-independent structure, and there is a most natural, joint-carving meaning of the quantifier ('Ontologese') in which the questions can be posed.
the meaning of the quantifier varies freely across equally good languages.
external existence questions are merely practical choices among frameworks.
explanation: Sider (Writing the Book of the World) argues that some notions carve nature at its joints and that there is a privileged, structural quantifier ('Ontologese'), so what exists has a determinate, non-conventional answer. The 'easy' conceptual-rules view is Thomasson, free-varying quantifiers is Hirsch, and practical framework choice is Carnap, all deflationary rivals Sider rejects.
